messageValues.message:
=You plan literature searches for GymRamp, an education and certification platform for the fitness, wellness, recovery and rejuvenation industries. Current date: {{ $now.toISODate() }}.

Produce search queries for Europe PMC, which uses boolean syntax: AND, OR, NOT, parentheses and "quoted phrases". Do not use field tags.

Rules:
- 3 to 5 queries. Each must be specific enough to return relevant human research, not everything mentioning a keyword.
- Cover different angles: effectiveness for exercise recovery or performance, use in healthy or athletic populations, safety and contraindications, mechanisms, and practical protocols.
- Include common synonyms of the modality inside OR groups.
- Prefer terms used in sports science and exercise physiology.
- year_floor: the earliest publication year worth teaching from, normally 8 to 12 years ago.
- trials_query: 2 to 4 plain words for searching a clinical trial registry.
- core_terms: 2 to 8 lowercase names of the modality itself, including synonyms and abbreviations (for red light therapy: photobiomodulation, red light, near-infrared, low-level laser, lllt). A record that mentions none of them is discarded, so include every common name but never generic words like exercise or recovery.
- context_terms: 4 to 10 lowercase words that mark a record as relevant to GymRamp learners rather than to clinical medicine (for example exercise, athletes, muscle, soreness, performance, training, recovery, fitness). Records containing them rank higher.

Return the json object only.

parameters.query:
WITH input AS (
  SELECT * FROM jsonb_to_recordset($1::jsonb) AS x(
    source_key text, source_type text, doi text, pmid text, pmcid text, nct_id text, title text,
    authors jsonb, journal text, year int, pub_types jsonb, abstract text, url text, is_open_access boolean)
),
ins AS (
  INSERT INTO sources (source_key, source_type, doi, pmid, pmcid, nct_id, title, authors, journal,
                       year, pub_types, abstract, url, is_open_access, first_topic)
  SELECT source_key, source_type, doi, pmid, pmcid, nct_id, title, COALESCE(authors, '[]'), journal,
         year, COALESCE(pub_types, '[]'), abstract, url, COALESCE(is_open_access, false), $2
  FROM input
  ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
  RETURNING id, source_key
),
run AS (
  INSERT INTO research_runs (topic, trigger, found, new_sources)
  VALUES ($2, $3, (SELECT count(*) FROM input), (SELECT count(*) FROM ins))
  RETURNING id
),
resolved AS (
  SELECT i.source_key, COALESCE(n.id, e.id) AS id, (n.id IS NOT NULL) AS is_new
  FROM input i
  LEFT JOIN ins n ON n.source_key = i.source_key
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT s.id FROM sources s
    WHERE s.source_key = i.source_key
       OR (i.doi IS NOT NULL AND lower(s.doi) = lower(i.doi))
       OR (i.pmid IS NOT NULL AND s.pmid = i.pmid)
       OR (i.nct_id IS NOT NULL AND s.nct_id = i.nct_id)
    LIMIT 1
  ) e ON true
)
SELECT (SELECT id FROM run) AS run_id,
       COALESCE((SELECT json_agg(row_to_json(r)) FROM resolved r), '[]'::json) AS rows,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM ins) AS new_count;

meta.description: Sub-workflow. Searches Europe PMC + ClinicalTrials.gov for a topic, ranks by evidence strength, upserts every source into Postgres (dedupe by DOI/PMID/NCT) and returns an evidence pack with E01.. markers and computed citations. IN: topic, audience, search_hint, since_date, trigger, max_sources, config. OUT: { topic, run_id, found_total, new_count, evidence[] }. Writes: sources, research_runs.
